subject.title: Core hardening tracker: converge duplicated runtime invariants onto single owners

question: Should this issue remain the canonical umbrella for the listed core-hardening seams, with each row requiring separate owner approval and a focused linked PR?
rationale: The protected tracker spans several compatibility-sensitive architecture owners, and deciding which centralizations are valuable versus intentionally distinct requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep bounded umbrella
options.body: Retain this issue as the roadmap while requiring separate owner-reviewed PRs and evidence for every seam.

options.title: Split approved rows
options.body: Create dedicated issues only for approved seams, preserve the completed-row links, and then retire the umbrella.

options.title: Defer broad hardening
options.body: Pursue only rows tied to concrete user-facing drift and pause the remaining architecture program.

recommendation.title: Keep bounded umbrella
recommendation.body: Retain this issue as the roadmap while requiring separate owner-reviewed PRs and evidence for every seam.

likelyOwner.reason: The central current-main surfaces largely trace to their recent commit, making them the strongest available owner for the architecture-direction decision.
